articles.title: GTA 6 Won't Be 'Too Specific About Any Particular Person, Event, or Movement,' Rockstar Says GTA Has Never Focused on 'National Politics'
articles.summary: Rockstar apparently isn’t interested in making a political statement in GTA 6, a game about love, passion, and the shrinking of the American dream. In the company’s defense, its reasoning is sound.
body: The line is drawn at political satire via real-world moments. If GTA 6 had created an NPC called Melon Husk who shoots rockets into space and is a bit weird, by the time it came out it wouldn’t have factored in all the horrible stuff that character’s real-life counterpart has done since. These games take a long time to make, and no one wants to be as dated as a Borderlands gag.

"If you go back to previous GTAs, there's never really been much focus on national politics," Rupert Humphries, senior vice president of narrative of Rockstar, told Love Magazine. "The rise of Homeland Security and the Patriot Act were pretty central to GTA 4, but that was mainly because post-9/11 New York was a real frontline for those issues.

“Because we are trying to make games that feel very specific to the moment they are released, but at the same time, not reflective of the exact world we live in, we don't want to be too specific about any particular person, event, movement or anything like that.”

articles.summary: Star Wars: Galactic Racer is finally out, and so far, it might just be one of the best Star Wars games ever made. The new racing game has an attractive MSRP of $60, but if you're looking to grab it for the low price of nothing, you can play it for free through Amazon Luna starting today.
body: Amazon has announced that Prime members can stream the single-player campaign for free through Amazon Luna. "We've always believed Luna players deserve to be in the action from day one, and Star Wars: Galactic Racer makes that a reality for the first time,” Jeff Gattis, Head of Gaming at Amazon, said in a blog post. "Luna players can jump into the single-player campaign today without needing to own a console or wait for a lengthy download. It's exactly the kind of experience we want to deliver on Luna, and we think players are going to love it."

If you're unfamiliar with it, Amazon Luna is a cloud gaming service and platform available to Prime members. A rotating selection of games appears every month through Luna, and members can also claim several downloadable PC games. These can be redeemed through storefronts like the Epic Games Store and GOG. Last month was particularly good, as members could claim several of Id Software's critically acclaimed Doom games, including the 2016 reboot and Doom Eternal.

articles.title: As Halo Moves to Activision, Halo Studios Writers Tease What Might Have Been
articles.summary: Following the launch of Halo: Campaign Evolved, Halo Studios has put out a blog post detailing plans for the future of Master Chief’s story. It’s an interesting look at where the series might have gone, prior to the recent announcement that Activision is now the shepherd of the Halo series.
body: The next Halo game was reportedly still years away, but the blog post, penned by Halo franchise writer Alex Wakeford, gives us a peek behind the curtain with hints about the studio’s plans, but also an attempt at canonizing a story that’s been told through games, remakes, books, and TV. You can check out the blog post for its list of retcons and continuity clarifications.

While the majority of the blog was written prior to the Xbox reshuffle, when Halo Studios thought the series was still in its hands, there are addendums written prior to the news breaking. At one point, Wakeford joked that you’ll have to wait until next week to find out more about the Sacristan Order, before dropping a note: “This joke sure took on new dimensions after last week's news.”

Elsewhere, Wakeford talked about the next novel by Troy Denning, titled Halo: Fireteam Noble. “Many have been asking whether this novel will still be releasing,” Wakeford said. “To this we can say that it is absolutely our intent to see this project cross the finish line. Troy has written a fantastic story and a good chunk of the editorial process has been conducted.”

articles.title: Charlie Brown's Halloween Special Still Rules Over Peanuts Christmas in 1 Way
articles.summary: Come Christmas time, if you’re looking for some wholesome (but not sickeningly so), feel-good, family entertainment, you can take your pick. While A Charlie Brown Christmas is one of the best sources of that warm holiday feeling, if you didn’t want to fork over the money to buy the special from…
body: A Charlie Brown Christmas was a major success when it first aired on CBS in 1965 and it immediately led to the production of two more specials, Charlie Brown's All Stars!, which aired during the summer of 1966, and It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown which debuted 60 years ago, on Oct. 27, 1966. In the tradition of “If it ain’t broke, don’t fix it,” the Halloween special had the same crew as the Christmas special. Charles Schulz himself penned the script, Bill Melendez directed it, Vince Guaraldi provided the music, and even the same voice actors returned to play the Peanuts gang.

The Halloween special also managed to expand things a little bit by not just playing the same notes, bringing in some staple moments from the comic strip that weren’t included in the Christmas special. For example, It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown was the first time in animation that Snoopy as the World War I Flying Ace was depicted. It was also the first time the Charlie Brown football gag was realized in animation.

articles.title: Supermassive Games suffers layoffs as more than 70 developers seem to have left the company this week
articles.summary: Supermassive Games - the developer behind games such as Directive 8020 and the original Until Dawn - seems to have lost over 70 staff today as part of widespread layoffs at the company.
body: Supermassive Games previously announced these were coming in August. In a statement posted to social media, the developer wrote: "We have made the difficult decision to begin a redundancy consultation process, which we anticipate will result in the loss of up to 75 of our colleagues. This is a necessary step to ensure the sustainability of our company."

It seems that this layoff process has concluded as of this week, as now-former IT and facilities director Frank Tindle announced his departure on LinkedIn with a fond farewell to other Supermassive staff in the same position as him.

"More than 70 brilliant people are leaving Supermassive: developers, artists, producers, QA, operations and more. Any studio would be lucky to have them. If you're hiring, DM me and I'll make the introduction."

This isn't the first time Supermassive has suffered job cuts in recent memory. Back in July 2025, the studio announced up to 36 employees would be laid off, claiming these cuts would allow them to "adapt our team structure to better align with recent industry changes". This resulted in the delay of Directive 8020, a game that would go on to release this May.

articles.title: Evangelion Creator Returns to Direct Another Sci-Fi Anime Classic
articles.summary: In October 1974, one of the most influential anime and sci-fi series of all time aired for the first time in Japan: Space Battleship Yamato, known in the United States as Star Blazers.
body: Hideaki Anno, the creator of the Neon Genesis Evangelion franchise, will be directing an anime movie titled Space Battleship Yamato √2199, produced by Anno's own Studio Khara in collaboration with Production I.G. This is only the latest in a long list of Yamato announcements, as in 2024 the franchise also released the first in a series of seven remake films, Be Forever Yamato: Rebel 3199. Anno's movie, however, seems to be taking a different direction from the remake movies.

Announced through an official website and an X profile, Space Battleship Yamato √2199 marks the first collaboration between Anno's Studio Khara and Production I.G. In 2024, during an event held for the 50th anniversary of the series, the director briefly mentioned being involved in a project in the Yamato franchise. On that occasion, Anno stated how influential Space Battleship Yamato had been to shape his taste and career: "Without this work, anime would have been in a different form than it is today." In a recent interview for Monthly Newtype, Anno mentioned that he aims to "create a Yamato that embodies our prayers and wishes for both the next generation and our own."

articles.title: 11 Most Essential White Cards Every Magic: The Gathering Player Should Know
articles.summary: White has always been one of the easiest colors in Magic: The Gathering to misunderstand. On the surface, it’s deceptively simple: armies of little creatures, life gain, exile-based removal, and an unhealthy obsession with justice and righteousness.
body: Guided by head designer Mark Rosewater’s core philosophy of peace through absolute structure, white demands that individual advantage yield to universal law and symmetry. Iconic cards like Swords to Plowshares, Wrath of God, and Balance weaponize this dogmatic pursuit of equality, razing entire battlefields or taxing every action to enforce total compliance.

Calling something “quintessentially white,” however, doesn’t mean it’s the strongest card ever printed in the color wheel. Some of these entries are ancient by Magic standards, while others represent how dramatically white has evolved over the years. In no particular order, these are the 11 best cards that capture white’s color identity in Magic.

articles.title: Tarae: The Unbound seems to get what makes a good ARPG, but crunchy combat aside, can it rise to the likes of Diablo and Path of Exile?
articles.summary: Who doesn't love a good top-down ARPG; a solid dungeon-crawler with visceral action and real punchy combat that sticks in your teeth like toffee? Aside from Diablo and Path of Exile, there aren't as many out there as I'd like.
body: Tarae is an isometric action game rooted deeply in Buddhist mythology, and while its demo might be relatively short, it's immediately clear Boundary understands the most important quality of ARPGs: making combat feel good. That starts with a choice between three distinct classes, and, in the demo, I pick the Samurai; a melee-focused fighter who's all about getting up close and wreaking havoc.

You've a dodge roll, a limited stamina bar, and a few healing potions to see you through the dangerous world ahead. And each swing of your sword comes with satisfyingly hefty audio-visual feedback. But it's more than simple slicing and dicing, and includes an intriguing set of abilities that elevates the experience.
points: Who doesn't love a good top-down ARPG; a solid dungeon-crawler with visceral action and real punchy combat that sticks in your teeth like toffee?
Aside from Diablo and Path of Exile, there aren't as many out there as I'd like.

articles.title: "This is Call of Duty's definitive extraction shooter experience" - Infinity Ward details the new DMZ mode in Modern Warfare 4
articles.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 studio Infinity Ward is betting big on DMZ - the game's extraction shooter mode - becoming another major pillar of the series. In a wide-ranging blog post and developer diary, we learn more about the studio's goals, and how the upcoming DMZ builds on 2022's Modern…
body: Infinity Ward hopes the new DMZ mode will be an important addition to the genre, referring to the mode several times as the "action extraction shooter", emphasising the mode's focus on combat and engagement over menu navigation and looting - two things synonymous with other extraction shooters. Those elements do exist in DMZ, but from what the developer showed of it, the UI is designed to allow for speedy navigation with clear icons and a smooth flow.

DMZ has its own separate progression from the rest of the game, featuring 70 levels you can only climb through by playing it. It also, unsurprisingly, has its own separate economy of cash and crafting materials that persist between rounds, essentially making it a game within a game. That said, certain elements - such as weapon progression, are shared with Modern Warfare 4's multiplayer modes and battle royale mode Warzone.

articles.title: After 12 years, Ultra Street Fighter IV gets not one, but two connection-stabilising rollback netcode mods aaaand they're both made using Claude
articles.summary: Street Fighter IV, the game that basically revived the fighting game genre back in 2009 and gave birth (not literally) to a new subset of players lovingly referred to as ‘09ers’, saw its final iteration in 2014’s Ultra Street Fighter IV.
body: To quickly explain why the different netcode matters, delay-based netcode handles latency issues by variably delaying inputs to match unstable connection, while rollback netcode removes this delay by accepting inputs immediately and then reversing the game state (rolling back) if the connection instability causes inconsistency between players. All of this to say, rollback has become the industry standard for its stability since the mid 2010s, leaving delay-based to rot in input-eating hell.

The prospect of USFIV being modded to have rollback stapled on should be cause for celebration — as it initially was with a seemingly abandoned mod from a few years ago by Wren theenby — but, as continues to happen with these fanmade mods, remakes, recomps and decomps in the current era, both of the new projects were made with generative AI. I really wish this wasn’t just the way things are now.

articles.title: Halloween’s First DLC Reveals Even The Bad Sequels Will Get Some Love
articles.summary: Halloween's first paid DLC is coming on October 27 in the form of a new skin for the game's killer, Michael Myers, and it's pulling from a source you might not expect: Halloween 5: The Revenge of Michael Myers.
body: It may seem odd to jump to the fifth movie for the game's first DLC, but it's not the only piece of new content coming that day. There's also a second skin coming for Big Mike, borrowing from his look in the legacy sequel Halloween (2018). Each skin will run you $10.

Survivor mains also have new things to look forward to, including two new characters, Michelle and Eugene, as well as Civilian Costumes Pack 1, which includes 14 outfits--one for each survivor character--and 42 colorings, or "tints." The new survivors will also go for $10, though that's for the pair, not for each of them, while the new styles and colors will be--you guessed it--$10 for the set. This content drop is the first of several coming to the game in its first year, development studio Illfonic said.

articles.title: Amid Uncharted 5 Rumors, Nathan Drake Actor Says He Would Come Back, But With One Catch
articles.summary: One of actor Nolan North's most famous roles is that of Nathan Drake in Naughty Dog's Uncharted franchise, but he wrapped things up with 2016's Uncharted 4: A Thief's End.
body: “110%. Absolutely. I think it would be one of the biggest games ever if they decided to do it. It just depends if Sony wants to make money," he said at Gamergy in Puerto Rico prior to the recent rumors of Uncharted 5 ( via DomTheBomb ). "I absolutely would. I try to stay in shape just in case. I can't see a scenario where I would say no. I always keep out hope."
North went on to clarify that he has not heard anything about a new Uncharted game where he might be asked to come back, but he thinks it would be a good business decision for Sony.
"It is a business-my god, can you imagine if they did? It would be the biggest announcement in gaming. I don't think that's hyperbole. I think that's true," he said.
North said he enjoyed working with Naughty Dog over the years on the four main Uncharted games, and that's part of why he would be up to come back.

body: The wait is over! Our newest Support Hero is here with the arrival of Doctrine. Freed from his volcanic prison by Doomfist himself, this sinister foe can manipulate life using his Eternal Scepter and mechanical drones, while also empowering each ability with his signature Infuse.

Break into Watchpoint: Grímsvötn - the Icelandic prison that once held Doctrine and Doomfist, and our first new Escort Map since Overwatch 2 launched. Battle your way through fire and ice as the final chapter in the Reign of Talon starts right here.

The Halloween mayhem continues this year with our newest event, Mystery Madness: Graveyard Games. You’ll start off as a random Hero and unlock random new powers each time you die. Complete chilling challenges to collect Offerings and help summon the next Hero into the madness.
